s: A company runs a proprietary stateless ETL application on an Amazon EC2 Linux instance. The application is a Linux binary, and the source code cannot be modified. The application is singlethreaded, uses 2 GB of RAM. and is highly CPU intensive The application is scheduled to run every 4 hours and runs for up to 20 minutes A solutions architect wants to revise the architecture for the solution. Which strategy should the solutions architect use?
o: Use AWS Lambda to run the application. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to invoke the Lambda function every 4 hours.
Use AWS Batch to run the application. Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to invoke the AWS Batch job every 4 hours.
Use AWS Fargate to run the application. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke the Fargate task every 4 hours.
Use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to run the application. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy and run the application every 4 hours.
e: step function could run a scheduled task when triggered by eventbrige, but why would you add that layer of complexity just to run aws batch when you could directly invoke it through eventbridge. The link provided - https://aws.amazon.com/pt/blogs/compute/orchestrating-high-performance computing-with-aws-step-functions-and-aws-batch/ makes sense only for HPC, this is a single instance that needs to be run

w.y: The binary cannot be changed, runs for up to 20 minutes every 4 hours, and needs 2 GB of RAM. Packaging it in a container and running it as a Fargate task started by an EventBridge schedule removes the always-on instance, and there is no time limit.

o.A: Lambda has a 15-minute limit, and CloudWatch Logs cannot schedule invocations.
o.B: AWS Batch works but adding Step Functions just to schedule it is more than needed; EventBridge can schedule directly.
o.C: Correct: a scheduled Fargate task runs the unmodified binary for 20 minutes and costs nothing in between.
o.D: CodeDeploy is a deployment tool, not a scheduler, and Spot interruptions could kill the job.
